nary_nodes.label: Definition of Solar Eclipse
evidence: A solar eclipse happens when the Moon passes between the Sun and Earth, blocking some or all of the Sun's light and casting a shadow on our planet.

evidence: As seen from the UK, the Sun, Moon and Earth were not quite directly in line.

nary_nodes.label: Sun, Moon, Earth perfectly aligned
evidence: At roughly 19:30 BST (20:30 local time), the Sun, Moon and Earth were perfectly aligned - a total eclipse.

nary_nodes.label: Yasmin Catricheo Travels for Eclipse
evidence: Chilean scientist Yasmin Catricheo, travelled thousands of miles to A Coruña, north-west Spain for the event.

nary_nodes.type_justification: No suitable schema.org class exists; this describes an event of travel.

nary_nodes.label: Totality was exciting and indescribable
evidence: "At the totality, everyone was cheering and sharing the excitement of what we were seeing. No words could describe the feeling," she said.

nary_nodes.label: Total solar eclipse global frequency
evidence: A total solar eclipse happens somewhere on Earth every 18 months or so.

nary_nodes.label: Total solar eclipse local rarity
evidence: But they are much rarer for any given place, only occurring once in roughly 400 years.

nary_nodes.label: Corona definition
evidence: The light coming from the darkness was the Sun's corona - superheated jets of gas thrown thousands of miles out into space.

nary_nodes.label: Prominences definition
evidence: small loops of pink gas called prominences following the Sun's turbulent magnetic field.

nary_nodes.label: Total eclipse is cosmological coincidence
evidence: The fact that we get to experience a total eclipse at all is an incredible cosmological coincidence.

nary_nodes.label: Sun-Earth vs Moon-Earth distance
evidence: The Sun is 150 million kilometres (93 million miles) away from the Earth - 400 times further away than the Moon.

nary_nodes.label: Moon and Sun apparent size explanation
evidence: But because the diameter of the Moon is 400 times less than the Sun's, they appear exactly the same size in our sky.

nary_nodes.label: Hypothetical conditions for no total eclipse
evidence: If the Moon was slightly smaller or its orbit was a little further away from the Earth then we would never see a total eclipse.

nary_nodes.label: Upcoming golden age of total eclipses
evidence: We're about to enter a "golden age" of total solar eclipses between 2026 and 2028.

nary_nodes.label: Future Total Solar Eclipses (2026-2028)
evidence: Eclipse chasers can travel around the world to be wowed by the spectacle of three total solar eclipses in the next couple of years.
